: Assertion: 'REENT malloc succeeded' failed. /build/gnu-tools-for-stm32_9-2020-q2-update.20201001-1621/src/newlib/newlib/libc/stdlib/rand.c:78
```

**How To Reproduce**

1. Generate project using TouchGFX Designer.

2. UI Template used from the designer was TouchGFX Demo 3(Since the display resolution of the board is 320 by 240)

3. From the main screen add a widget(button with label)

4. Configure interaction of the button. Trigger: 'Button is clicked', Action: call virtual function 'button1Clicked'

5. STM32CubeIDE: Import generated project.

6. Run CubeMX from the CubeIDE. Configure peripherals, onboard LED.

7. Implement function 'button1Clicked'
   ```cpp
   void MainView::button1Clicked()
   {
     HAL_GPIO_TogglePin(LED_LD3_GPIO_Port, LED_LD3_Pin);
     HAL_GPIO_TogglePin(LED_LD4_GPIO_Port, LED_LD4_Pin);
     
     // Set Random Color
     auto randColor = rand();
     dlogln("%s: rand = %08Xh", __PRETTY_FUNCTION__, randColor);
     uint8_t rgb_r = randColor & 0xFF;
     uint8_t rgb_g = (randColor >> 8) & 0xFF;
     uint8_t rgb_b = (randColor >> 16) & 0xFF;
     buttonWithLabel1.setLabelColor(touchgfx::Color::getColorFrom24BitRGB(rgb_r, rgb_g, rgb_b));
     buttonWithLabel1.invalidate();
   }
   ```
   
8. Build project. Program firmware binary.

9. Run the board.

10. Click the button widget.

11. Assertion fail message is printed and TouchGFX task halts.

comments.author: ALABSTM
comments.body:
Hello @WilheJo,

Thank you for this report. The link you provided redirects to a bug description indicating SHA-1 of two commits. Is this related to our source files or yours? In case it is related to ours, would you please provide more precise description about the bug and the fix? Thank you again.

With regards,

comments.author: WilheJo
comments.body:
It seems that there are several recent Linux Kernel releases which have broken ACM drivers.

This report has been filed since it was unclear if the USB CDC implementation on the STM32 or the Linux Kernel trigger/contain a bug.

The commits referenced in the linked bug report above contain some description on the origin of the bug. It seems that some refactoring due to circular dependencies have led to this problem.

In the end, there's a good likelihood that some of the several releases (5.10.28-5.10.32 are definitly effected; the bug is/was also present in the 5.11 and 5.12 kernel tree) will cause troubles to users. Hence I linked the bugzilla report which references the patch which can be cherrypicked from the usb-next tree to recompile a fixed kernel.

Regards

comments.author: ALABSTM
comments.body:
Hi @WilheJo,

Thank you for all these details and for having reported. If I understand correctly, this issue is rather related to the Linux Kernel rather than to our USB CDC implementation. As a fix, users can cherry-pick the patch from the [usb-next](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/gregkh/usb.git/log/?h=usb-next) branch.

Thank you again for this initiative. Users facing the problem you reported could land here and find the fix you proposed.

With regards,

Hi @fpistm,

Thank you for this report.

Referring to the datasheet and product description, the GPIOG and GPIOF are available in packages **LQFP144** and **UFBGA144** which are provided with **STM32F412Zx** part number. 

The HAL driver is aligned with the MCU specification. However, the CMSIS file should be updated and the section below should be removed from the stm32f412vx.h CMSIS device file as STM32F412Vx devices do not support GPIOG and GPIOF.

```diff
  #define GPIOE_BASE            (AHB1PERIPH_BASE + 0x1000UL)
- #define GPIOF_BASE            (AHB1PERIPH_BASE + 0x1400UL)
- #define GPIOG_BASE            (AHB1PERIPH_BASE + 0x1800UL)
  #define GPIOH_BASE            (AHB1PERIPH_BASE + 0x1C00UL)
```

With regards,

title: PLL can't be updated when PLL is already used for sysclock
body:
**Setup**
Custom board containing STM32F439VI with external 8MHz crystal
FW_F4 V1.26.1
Toolchain: SW4STM32
Cube MX version: 6.2.0

**Bug**
Bug occurs when setting the PLLCLK as source for the SYSCLK in CubeMX, using 8MHz HSE as source for PLL, as shown below.
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/79446929/113304935-cccaea00-9302-11eb-9f85-8bd2db331183.png)


**Analysis**
The `HAL_RCC_OscConfig(&RCC_OscInitStruct)` call in main.c (in `SystemClock_Config`) fails. This failure is caused because the (I assume by default) input for SYSCLK is already set to PLLCLK, which is checked on line 467 of `stm32f4_hal_rcc.c` (`if(__HAL_RCC_GET_SYSCLK_SOURCE() != RCC_CFGR_SWS_PLL)`. This check is done because the code within that if disables the PLL, which is not possible according to the reference manual when SYSCLK = PLLCLK.
Because of this, PLL is not set to the new settings defined in `SystemClock_Config` but rather goes to either line 544 or 552  ( `stm32f4_hal_rcc.c` )where the current PLL settings are checked against the user settings which obviously fails because the user settings are impossible to write in this case.

The issue can be circumvented by prepending `SystemClock_Config` with a call that sets the SYSCLK to HSI instead of PLLCLK.
I feel like this is a bug rather than expected behavior.

Further investigation shows that the STM32F439 is supposed to start with HSI as SYSCLK, which leads me to believe that the HAL is changing SYSCLK source before even SystemClock_Config
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/79446929/113389517-76a48800-9390-11eb-9eab-aa5e2f3ccc6e.png)

comments.author: chrisreedtech
comments.body:
Using STM32CubeMX 6.2.1 with a Nucleo F030R8 running STM32Cube FW_F0 1.11.2.

I had been getting a error in the following line in ```SystemClock_Config``` on all my Nucleo cores with a STOCK unmodified project generated from CubeMX.
```
  if (HAL_RCC_OscConfig(&RCC_OscInitStruct) != HAL_OK)
  {
    Error_Handler();
  }
```
Following @Glaciuse's tip, I added
```__HAL_RCC_SYSCLK_CONFIG(RCC_CFGR_SWS_HSI);```
in the User Code Begin section above ```SystemClock_Config()``` and the hard fault is no longer being thrown.

So thanks @glaciuse's for this as now I don't have to comment out ```Error_Handler();``` every time I regenerate code from MX!
Saves me a fair bit of time!

The interesting thing is, before I added this line, Any of my Nucleo boards would hard fault when set to use the internal PLL driven from the HSI (HSE not populated). If I commented out the ```Error_Handler();``` call so that it wouldn't trigger
the hard fault, the code would actually still work just fine (the best I can tell).

Also, switching the clock source in CubeMX to HSI instead of PLL driven by HSI, caused the error to also disappear without adding the line of code.

Hope this testing helps in some way

	mmw 0x40023800 0x01000000 0 ;# RCC_CR |= PLLON
	sleep 10                    ;# Wait for PLL to lock
	mmw 0x40023808 0x00001000 0 ;# RCC_CFGR |= RCC_CFGR_PPRE1_DIV2
	mmw 0x40023808 0x00000002 0 ;# RCC_CFGR |= RCC_CFGR_SW_PLL

	# Boost JTAG frequency
	adapter speed 8000
}
```

title: HAL USART Driver Error for STM32F4xx
body:
We are a startup working with STM32CubeF429 Discovery Kit. We downloaded the official STM32CubeIDE and generated code for USART peripheral. 

On compiling the code, we found an error in the driver file: stm32f4xx_hal.c in the following functions at bottom of this file: a) 'USART_Receive_IT()' and b) 'USART_TransmitReceive_IT()'. 

The error is minor that defined macros used in the body of these functions in the if-else block should contain 'USART' instead of 'UART' in them. As the files are for USART. This throws the error. As soon as we corrected this, the project compiled successfully. 

I thought the ST community should know as drivers should not be modified in general. Thank you. See the individual files as well.

[STM32CubeIDE- CubeHALF429 USART Driver Files.zip](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/files/6192046/STM32CubeIDE-.CubeHALF429.USART.Driver.Files.zip)

comments.body:
Hi @gionag,

The HardFault is due to a division by zero within the `SMBUS_SPEED_STANDARD(pclk1, hsmbus->Init.ClockSpeed)`  instruction called during the SMBUS initialization `HAL_SMBUS_Init()`. The `hsmbus->Init.ClockSpeed` is not initialized and keeps its default value which is zero.  Given that the `SMBUS_SPEED_STANDARD` macro will divide  `pclk1`  the `hsmbus->Init.ClockSpeed` a HardFault will be generated since `hsmbus->Init.ClockSpeed` is equal to zero.

This issue is rather related to the CubeIDE tool and particularly to the CubeMx tool used for the generation of the initialization code. Actually, aspects related to tools are not handled at GitHub level. They are rather treated at **ST Community** level, precisely within the **CubeMX** dedicated [section](https://community.st.com/s/topic/0TO0X000000BTr8WAG/stm32cubemx) and  **CubeIDE** dedicated [section](https://community.st.com/s/topic/0TO0X000000y2j7WAA/stm32cubeide). There, you may find posts that already raised the issue you are pointing out here. Otherwise, you can create a new post to submit your issue.

As this issue is not directly related to software component published within this repository (CMSIS, HAL, BSP, etc.) but rather to ecosystem (CubeMX tool, CubeIDE tool), please allow me to close it. Thank you for your comprehension.

comments.author: RKOUSTM
comments.body:
Hi @theadib,

I hope you are fine. Our development teams said your proposal could not be taken into consideration for the following reason:

>The modifying of VTOR is now only performed if USER_VECT_TAB_ADDRESS is activated (in the IDE or directly in the file). This is done on purpose as the memory remap is performed at boot, allows the vector table to be basically at address 0x00. So, if the user does not want to relocate it anywhere else, there is no need to access this register. More than that some products (like dual CPU ones) use the boot address from the option bytes, so having a generic way of setting VTOR is worse than letting the default configuration (option bytes set boot @ => that one is remapped @ 0x0)

Please allow me to close this issue now and thank you for your comprehension. We are looking forward to reading from you again.

With regards,

comments.author: ALABSTM
comments.body:
Hi @theadib,

Hope you are fine. Back to you about the points you raised:

> 1. please set the vector address register regardless of USER_VECT_TAB_ADDRESS
> 2. please test before setting VECT_TAB_OFFSET
> 3. however I do not really understand the use of USER_VECT_TAB_ADDRESS

Regarding point **1**, as explained by @RKOUSTM, the default value 0x00000000 of the `SCB->VOTR` register after a re-boot supposes the vector table is located at address 0x08000000, which is the default setting. Since address 0x08000000 is aliased 0x00000000 by default, access to the vector table will be correctly performed in case of interrupt.

This is why, in case this default setting is not to be changed by the user, there is no need to write-access the `SCB->VTOR` register during system initialization. Now, this also supposes, in case of a **custom** board, that pin `BOOT0` is connected to the `GND`. You can find more details in the reference manual.

Regarding points **2** and **3**, we do agree that, even with the new proposal, it is not yet possible to define the `VECT_TAB_OFFSET` at IDE- or Makefile-level. The point has been reported to our development teams. You can follow the progress [here](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeL0/pull/10).

With regards,

title: HAL_I2C_Mem_Read_IT routine causing interrupts to hang processor
body:
**Describe the set-up**
 * Custom board with STM32F417, external 8MHz crystal, system clock running at 168MHz
 * External battery with BQ27750 chipset connected to main processor on I2C1
 * Compiler: gcc-arm-none-eabi-7-2018-q2-update
 * [edit] I2C bus is running at 100KHz

**Describe the bug**
While doing an interrupt-driven I2C memory read operation, a 2-byte read from a device resulted in 137 individual interrupts.

**How To Reproduce**
1. Indicate the global behavior of your application project.
Multi-task FreeRTOS application that runs a periodic motion control loop and U/I. One task updates the battery indicator by polling every second to read multiple values from the TI BQ27750, using HAL_I2C_Mem_Read_IT. When this battery read happens, the other tasks in the system fail to meet their timing requirements because the processor gets bogged down servicing I2C interrupts for up to 500us

2. The modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem (Driver, BSP, MW ...).
Driver module, specifically stm32f4xx_hal_i2c.c

3. How we can reproduce the problem.
This is very reproducible on my device. Simply do a 2-byte read from an I2C device and watch the interrupt traffic.

**Additional context**
First analysis: After transmission of the memory address to be read, the buffer interrupt is being left enabled while the device is waiting for the restart to be processed, causing the TXE bit to trigger interrupts more than 40 times. Additionally, in the case of a 2-byte read, the buffer interrupt is being left enabled after the restart bit is processed. Since the driver is waiting for the BTF flag for a 2-byte read, the RX bit will trigger interrupts repeatedly which will be no-ops as they pass through the code.  

**Screenshots**
I've got a log of all the interrupt activity complete with SR2, SR1, CR1, CR2 activity. 
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1GoMnkRJhdg2N3yBubqI4ouFaiV02xWcZ7q9KeIoLRdk/edit?usp=sharing

comments.author: ASELSTM
jasonbraley
comments.body:
Hi, @ASELSTM 

I finally got a chance to try the proposed patch (I had to upgrade my code base to support 1.25.0 first), and I'm still seeing the blocking interrupt behavior even when the restart bit is not being repeatedly set. I've updated the Google Sheet that I linked to in the defect description with the two new tabs: one of the behavior on 1.25.0 before the patch and one after. The behavior looks identical to me except that now the EventCount field gets set to 3. 

If you don't mind me offering my analysis of the situation, I think the root cause of the issue is not that the restart bit gets set multiple times. While the memory read address is being transmitted, the data buffer will naturally empty into the shift register, forcing the TXE bit to be high, which will trigger the buffer interrupt. Since we have no more to transmit (we just wanted to transmit the address), there's nothing else to do while we wait for the address to finish. But since the TXE bit is still high and the buffer interrupt is enabled while that's happening, the system will just interrupt over and over and over again, hanging the processor.

Similarly, once we start receiving, in the case of a 2 byte read there's no work to do in the driver during the interrupts when the RXNE bit is set; the driver is instead waiting for the BTF flag interrupt (one byte in the data register, one byte in the shift register) to complete the operation. The buffer interrupt is being left enabled in this case as well, causing repeated entry into the interrupt handler (which does nothing if I'm reading it right) before returning and interrupting again.

I've patched around this issue (it reduces the interrupt traffic considerably) in my own code by disabling the buffer interrupt when the restart bit is set and re-enabling it if the XferCount is !=2. 

Please feel free to ask any more questions, and I'll gather any data that you need as soon as I can.

comments.body:
Hello everyone,

Thank you all for your comments and feedback.

Regarding `UserTxBufferFS[]` and `UserRxBufferFS[]`, it is normal to have them in the code generated by Cube MX. Indeed, the tool is intended to generate the "skeleton" of what is intended to be a **standard** USB application.
These very buffers are the one intended to be used by the user for their application. In case the user want to define their owns, up to them to customize the generated code. From the tool perspective, however, we **shall keep** these buffers.

Regarding further uses of these two buffers, you can notice some from the [CDC_Standalone](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/tree/master/Projects/STM32469I_EVAL/Applications/USB_Device/CDC_Standalone) application, taken as an example.

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/2f3b26f16559f7af495727a98253067a31182cfc/Projects/STM32469I_EVAL/Applications/USB_Device/CDC_Standalone/Src/usbd_cdc_interface.c#L239-L241
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/2f3b26f16559f7af495727a98253067a31182cfc/Projects/STM32469I_EVAL/Applications/USB_Device/CDC_Standalone/Src/usbd_cdc_interface.c#L269

Regarding both calls below, they are necessary. Otherwise, eventual later calls to `USBD_CDC_TransmitPacket()` would fail.

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/2f3b26f16559f7af495727a98253067a31182cfc/Projects/STM32469I_EVAL/Applications/USB_Device/CDC_Standalone/Src/usbd_cdc_interface.c#L124-L126

To conclude, parameter `length` of the `USBD_CDC_SetTxBuffer()` function does not define the size of the buffer. This latter is defined by the `APP_TX_DATA_SIZE` macro and **can be changed from the Cube MX GUI**.

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/2f3b26f16559f7af495727a98253067a31182cfc/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Device_Library/Class/CDC/Src/usbd_cdc.c#L857-L858

Rather, it indicates the length of the data **to be sent** when calling `USBD_CDC_TransmitPacket()`. Unfortunately, this parameter has not been described in the function's header. This will be done soon hopefully. This also explains why the `USBD_CDC_SetRxBuffer()` function does not have such one.

I hope my answers help. Otherwise, in case you have in mind some use-case you think relevant but not handled by Cube MX, please submit your proposal to the ST Community on the [section](https://community.st.com/s/topic/0TO0X000000BTr8WAG/stm32cubemx) dedicated to Cube MX.

With regards,

The length and buffer setup with USBD_CDC_SetTxBuffer is used in USBD_CDC_TransmitPacket. These two function calls are very tight connected with each other. I suggest that both USBD_CDC_SetTxBuffer and USBD_CDC_TransmitPacket should get a better description in the usbd_cdc.c file. Please explain the relation between them. One is to pass in the arguments, the other for trigger the action.

The UserTxBufferFS buffer isn't needed. If you for any reason want to keep it, please set the default size to zero (or one, if zero isn't posssible).

I would recommend to set the default size of UserRxBufferFS to CDC_DATA_FS_OUT_PACKET_SIZE.

The "USBD_CDC_SetTxBuffer(&hUsbDeviceFS, UserTxBufferFS, 0);" call in CDC_Init_FS is strange. Here you setup to send zero bytes and supply a pointer to the buffer where the bytes can be found. Zero bytes! To send zero bytes will be to send nothing. So nothing will be read from the buffer, i.e. the pointer isn't needed. It is actually very confusing to pass in a pointer in this situation. I recommend to set this argument to NULL. This call is good to have because it will initialize the two corresponding local variables to NULL and zero (they aren't initialize elsewhere). Note that if you do another change (I will describe next), this call can be removed.

Now about the pair **USBD_CDC_SetTxBuffer and USBD_CDC_TransmitPacket**, with a proposal. These can be **combine into one function** (as already written in this issue). Move the arguments from the first and put into the second. Remove the first function and only keep USBD_CDC_TransmitPacket. This by **keep the functionality** as today. This will make it more clear what it do and how it works. Please note that it still should be a asynchronous function, i.e. return quickly. It shouldn't stall. If the user want to wait for the transmition to finish, the callback function is available. By doing this change it will also be clear that the UserTxBufferFS buffer is never used. However that is in the cdc example app. The change to migrate these two functions to one is in the API to the drivers, i.e. effect many (to the better).

The pointer (buffer) setup in USBD_CDC_SetRxBuffer is used in USBD_CDC_ReceivePacket. Please note that this call will prepare the OUT Endpoint for reception, i.e. it will not actually do the reception. The buffer pointed to by this pointer needs to still be available after this call. The pointer sent in need to point to a buffer with space for atleast CDC_DATA_FS_OUT_PACKET_SIZE bytes. This isn't documented in usbd_cdc.c file at the USBD_CDC_SetRxBuffer function.

The row "USBD_CDC_SetRxBuffer(&hUsbDeviceFS, &Buf[0]);" in CDC_Receive_FS function isn't needed. I guess the reason for it to be where is to indicate that it is possible to change the receive buffer, i.e. where the next data will be written to. For example if you like to implement a circular buffer. If you like to keep this row, I suggest to have it comment away, maybe like this:
/* USBD_CDC_SetRxBuffer(&hUsbDeviceFS, &Buf[newWriteIndex]);  // Set new write position, for next data package. */

Please be aware of that usbd_cdc_if.c is only an example. This compare to some stuff we talking about which is on the other side of the API. This belong to the driver part and is much more important (USBD_CDC_* functions).

The usbd_cdc_if.c file contains half done example and maybe that is why it is so confusing. Note that code in this file are within "USER CODE" comments and exepected to be changed by the developer. Or you can actually skip this file and implement your own send and receive functions. Maybe it would be good with a better and longer description in top of this file.

PS. Please note that my example I wrote earlier about and the way of checking for the transmition to finish. Could be implemented differently by using the CDC_TransmitCplt_FS callback function. I didn't use it because it isn't available in the F1 version of this software (I began with a F103 device, moved over to a F401 and will go for a G0). Excuse me for showing this. However both way is working and checking the variable like I do, is actually also done usbd_cdc_if.c. 

_Thank you STM. The framework that can be created with your tool make it easy to get started with your MCU's. This with the cheap china boards make it possible to create a prototype quickly. It have been fun doing this and now I'm designing my own board._

comments.author: MichaelSweden
comments.body:
> @MichaelSweden, applications will be updated to ensure ongoing transfer has completed after each call to `USBD_CDC_TransmitPacket()`.

@ALABSTM I'm little concerned about this you wrote, it isn't clear for me. Is your intention to change the implementation of the USBD_CDC_TransmitPacket function or change example code that calling this function?

comments.author: ALABSTM
comments.body:
Hi @MichaelSweden,

I hope you are fine. Back to you about the points you raised:
1. Combining `USBD_CDC_SetTxBuffer()` and `USBD_CDC_TransmitPacket()` into one function.
2. Ensuring current packet transmission is finished before starting a new one.

Regarding point **1**, thank you very much for the detailed proposal you made and the time taken. Unfortunately, such an update would yield a **compatibility break**, which we cannot accept.

Regarding point **2**, our development teams replied such check is actually done. Below are the details.

I hope things are clearer now. Thank you again for your time and proposal.

With regards,

### Details about point 2

* Before any new packet transmission, check is made on `TxState` to ensure no previous packet is still being transferred `USBD_CDC_TransmitPacket()`.

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/2f3b26f16559f7af495727a98253067a31182cfc/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Device_Library/Class/CDC/Src/usbd_cdc.c#L909-L921

* In case a transmission is ongoing (**i.e.**, `TxState` is not zero)
  * No new transmission is initiated (lines `912` to `920` will not be executed).
  * The status `USBD_BUSY` is returned.

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/2f3b26f16559f7af495727a98253067a31182cfc/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Device_Library/Class/CDC/Src/usbd_cdc.c#L902

* Once the ongoing transfer is complete, an **interrupt** is triggered. The global interrupt request handler `OTG_FS_IRQHandler()` will be executed, which in turn will call the `HAL_PCD_IRQHandler()`.

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/2f3b26f16559f7af495727a98253067a31182cfc/Projects/STM32469I_EVAL/Applications/USB_Device/CDC_Standalone/Src/stm32f4xx_it.c#L160-L167

* Inside `HAL_PCD_IRQHandler()`, callback `HAL_PCD_DataInStageCallback()` is called...

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/2f3b26f16559f7af495727a98253067a31182cfc/Drivers/STM32F4xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f4xx_hal_pcd.c#L1186-L1190

* ... which in turn calls `USBD_LL_DataInStage()`, which in turn calls `USBD_CDC_DataIn()` within which `TxState` is cleared.
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/2f3b26f16559f7af495727a98253067a31182cfc/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Device_Library/Class/CDC/Src/usbd_cdc.c#L713

title: Move GPIO read/write/toggle into implementation into header
body:
I suggest to move the implementation of GPIO read/write/toggle into the header, so that the compiler (I assume GCC here) can optimize the code better without LTO. Without LTO, GCC will always insert a function call, which makes bit-banging or fast GPIO polling slower than necessary. For fast bit-banging or fast GPIO polling the overhead from the function calls actually create a measurable difference in speed.

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/b95577991ef8891c62c41e0845903e182cdf60d3/Drivers/STM32F4xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f4xx_hal_gpio.c#L377



Side note regarding LTO:

The current CubeIDE ships with a bug, so that LTO can only be used in conjunction with a workaround, I already posted about that here: https://community.st.com/s/question/0D53W00000MjO4DSAV/workaround-for-gcc-lto-bug
Unfortunately, there was no respone from ST.

title: Buffer overrun in USB_WritePacket if length not multiple of 4
body:
If the input length is not a multiple of 4, the function overruns the buffer by 3, 2 or 1 byte.
This could trigger an exception (HardFault/BusFault), e.g. if one passes a buffer pointing to the last byte in RAM and length=1.

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/b95577991ef8891c62c41e0845903e182cdf60d3/Drivers/STM32F4xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f4xx_ll_usb.c#L965

Other devices are possible affected as well.

title: RAM optimization for USB CDC
body:
The following declaration wastes 448 Byte of RAM on all devices where CDC is used with a USB FS spec.
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/2d5b78e2da98fb44e028d87f4ff815427991affc/Middlewares/ST/STM32_USB_Device_Library/Class/CDC/Inc/usbd_cdc.h#L113

The documentation suggests you could modify ```CDC_DATA_HS_MAX_PACKET_SIZE``` but that would only be a workaround.

Possible fix:
```c
typedef struct
{
#ifdef USBD_NO_HS          /* can be set by cubeMX or provided by user as project configuration */
   uint32_t data[CDC_DATA_FS_MAX_PACKET_SIZE / 4U];      /* Force 32bits alignment */
#else
   uint32_t data[CDC_DATA_HS_MAX_PACKET_SIZE / 4U];      /* Force 32bits alignment */
#endif
```

One could also query the ```#define USE_USB_FS``` which is used in usbd_core.c .

comments.author: ALABSTM
comments.body:
Hi @jrahlf,

Thank you for your proposal. It will be logged into our internal database so our development teams consider it in the frame of a future version of the library.

As you also suggested, macro `USE_USB_FS` could be used as shown below:

```diff
typedef struct
{
+#ifdef USE_USB_FS
+  uint32_t data[CDC_DATA_FS_MAX_PACKET_SIZE / 4U];      /* Force 32-bit alignment */
+#else
  uint32_t data[CDC_DATA_HS_MAX_PACKET_SIZE / 4U];      /* Force 32-bit alignment */
+#endif /* USE_USB_FS */
```

With regards,

I created a STM32F4 project which uses USB FS with CDC and the #define does not exist. It is however used in `usbd_core.c`. In the debugger I see that the HS descriptor is used, even though the USB is FS only.

```c

  pdev->pConfDesc = (void *)pdev->pClass->GetFSConfigDescriptor(&len);
#else /* USE_USB_HS */
  pdev->pConfDesc = (void *)pdev->pClass->GetHSConfigDescriptor(&len);
#endif /* USE_USB_FS */
```

This seems like a bug to me?
It still works nicely so nobody has noticed it before. Seems like the USB driver or the computer driver somehow fixes this, otherwise the mismatch in packet length (512 vs 64) would cause problems.

1. The check condition is indeed always correct and the first statement is always executed so that stop is never generated. The condition should be corrected. However, the fix proposed will lead to the same behavior, the condition should be corrected differently. Our development team is working on this and will propose a correction. 


2.  In fact, `SMBUS_LAST_FRAME_NO_PEC` should be deleted from the condition which will be : 
```diff
-if ((CurrentXferOptions == SMBUS_NEXT_FRAME) || (CurrentXferOptions == SMBUS_FIRST_FRAME) || (CurrentXferOptions == SMBUS_LAST_FRAME_NO_PEC)) 
+if ((CurrentXferOptions == SMBUS_NEXT_FRAME) || (CurrentXferOptions == SMBUS_FIRST_FRAME)) 
```


3. The first callback call will be deleted to avoid calling `HAL_SMBUS_ErrorCallback` twice :

```diff
-HAL_SMBUS_ErrorCallback(hsmbus); 
 #if (USE_HAL_SMBUS_REGISTER_CALLBACKS == 1) 
     hsmbus->ErrorCallback(hsmbus); 
 #else 
     HAL_SMBUS_ErrorCallback(hsmbus); 
 #endif /* USE_HAL_SMBUS_REGISTER_CALLBACKS */ 
```


The fixes will be implemented and made available in a future release. Thank you once again for your contribution.

With regards,

title: Include file versioning for every file
body:
I frequently find example code and STM32 projects on the web using HAL files or middleware like USB. None of the files include version information, and it's almost impossible to find out what specific version a developer used. As a result, it's very hard to get things working since the changes from version to version are sometimes very significant.

I suggest creating a script or batch file in your production environment, so that every time you are ready for a release, you can include version information in the header of each file (where you now have the @file name.

Lack of versioning makes it impossible to reuse old code, and it's such a simple thing to implement

comments.author: RKOUSTM
comments.body:
Hi @robcazzaro,

First, allow me to thank you for your contribution. However, no plain for our technical team to treat this point where we want to avoid that each file is modified, artificially, with each version. Thank you once again for your contribution.

Please, allow me to close this issue. Thank you for your comprehension.

With regards,

comments.author: robcazzaro
comments.body:
First of all, thanks for the answer and considering this.

I can understand if you do not want to modify every header file for each release, even if it's a best practice almost universally used. But, at a minimum, you should include a version number for when the file is created, and update it every time it's edited/changed. That would still allow a user to understand which version was used in a specific example, even if it's a bit harder that way

With no versioning (as it's the case now), users cannot easily reuse and leverage examples available on the internet. It's becoming harder and harder to work with STM files, as there is no way to easily recreate a working example from publicly available code

Having no version number is really user-hostile.

title: STM32F412Cx USART3 contradiction between CMSIS and HAL
body:
**Caution**
The Issues are strictly limited for the reporting of problem encountered with the software provided in this project.
For any other problem related to the STM32 product, the performance, the hardware characteristics and boards, the tools the environment in general, please post a topic in the [ST Community/STM32 MCUs forum](https://community.st.com/s/group/0F90X000000AXsASAW/stm32-mcus).

**Describe the set-up**
Custom board with STM32F412CG.
Mbed OS 6.2.0 with GCC ARM 9-2020-q2-update

**Describe the bug**
Cannot link `serial_api`, since there is a contradiction between CMSIS and HAL:

In CMSIS `stm32f412cx.h` `USART3_BASE` is defined. 

In RCC HAL, USART3 functions are not defined for `STM32F412Cx`.

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/9f5ea7421d22c724516d00218b350d1e09a54a2c/Drivers/STM32F4xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32f4xx_hal_rcc_ex.h#L5448-L5449

This causes linker issues for example when trying to link `serial_api.o` of the STM HAL in Mbed OS due to these lines:

https://github.com/ARMmbed/mbed-os/blob/master/targets/TARGET_STM/serial_api.c#L246-L252

I believe this is not an Mbed issue but an HAL issue. 

**How To Reproduce**
Try to build an Mbed OS 6.2.0 project for STM32F412CG.

**Additional context**
It is fixed when `STM32F412Cx` is added to the conditions for all USART3 functions.

N.a.

title: does not stop USB device correctly in HAL_PCD_Stop()
body:
**Caution**
The Issues are strictly limited for the reporting of problem encountered with the software provided in this project.
For any other problem related to the STM32 product, the performance, the hardware characteristics and boards, the tools the environment in general, please post a topic in the [ST Community/STM32 MCUs forum](https://community.st.com/s/group/0F90X000000AXsASAW/stm32-mcus).

**Describe the set-up**
 * The board (either ST RPN reference or your custom board).
 * IDE or at least the compiler and its version.
I use STM32F437VGT powered by battery (not USB).
I use CubeMX for setup and Initialisation
USB_FS is  is configured as CDC device.
MX_USB_DEVICE_Init is called by application not by main().

**Describe the bug**
A clear and concise description of what the bug is.
After detecting the USB cable is detached the application calls usbd_core.c:USBD_DeInit() function.
The goal is to detach USB from the USB pins to avoid unneeded PULL UP voltage on that pins.

The Problem is that the function USBD_DeInit() aborts with errorr code halfway and does not release USB from USB Pins.
1) USBD_LL_Stop does report USBD_TIMEOUT instead USBD_OK
2) function return 
3)  USBD_LL_DeInit is not called
   that would lead to USB detach USB pins

**How To Reproduce**
1. Indicate the global behavior of your application project.
1) start main
2) attach USB cable
3) call MX_USB_DEVICE_Init() -> PC does enumeration
4) detach USB cable
5) call USBD_DeInit -> function returns halfway and does not call USBD_LL_DeInit

2. The modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem (Driver, BSP, MW ...).
**
1) in file stm32f4xx_ll_usb.c line:1070 function USB_StopDevice is wrongly implemented.
2) in file stm32f4xx_ll_usb.c line:477 function USB_FlushRxFifo is wrongly implemented.
3) in file stm32f4xx_ll_usb.c line:454 function USB_FlushTxFifo is wrongly implemented.
4) the silicon has defects
**

1)  does not respect the real number of endpoints in the specific device
```
HAL_StatusTypeDef USB_StopDevice(USB_OTG_GlobalTypeDef *USBx)
...
  /* Clear Pending interrupt */
  for (i = 0U; i < 15U; i++)
  {
    USBx_INEP(i)->DIEPINT = 0xFB7FU;
    USBx_OUTEP(i)->DOEPINT = 0xFB7FU;
  }
...
```
according to datasheet for STM32F437 on the FS device i is in range 0..3 and for HS device i in range 0..7
So there must be differentiation of FS and HS device and respect the range.

1) should ignore errors on stopping
```
HAL_StatusTypeDef USB_StopDevice(USB_OTG_GlobalTypeDef *USBx)
...
  /* Flush the FIFO */
  ret = USB_FlushRxFifo(USBx);
  if (ret != HAL_OK)
  {
    return ret;
  }

  ret = USB_FlushTxFifo(USBx,  0x10U);
  if (ret != HAL_OK)
  {
    return ret;
  }
```
The initial problem could be avoided if there is no test of return value on USB_FlushRxFifo(USBx) and USB_FlushTxFifo(USBx,  0x10U).
So please do not test the return in the StopDevice() function.

2)  the function deserves a synchronisation barrier and more testing
```
HAL_StatusTypeDef USB_FlushRxFifo(USB_OTG_GlobalTypeDef *USBx)
{
...
    }
    __DSB();
  }
  while ((USBx->GRSTCTL & USB_OTG_GRSTCTL_RXFFLSH) == USB_OTG_GRSTCTL_RXFFLSH);

  return HAL_OK;
}
```
also in the registerdescription is is pointed out that care must be taken when accessing the flush function is the fifo is still in use.
I do not see such test.

3) the function deserves a synchronisation barrier and more testing 
```
HAL_StatusTypeDef USB_FlushTxFifo(USB_OTG_GlobalTypeDef *USBx, uint32_t num)
...
    }
    __DSB();
  }
  while ((USBx->GRSTCTL & USB_OTG_GRSTCTL_TXFFLSH) == USB_OTG_GRSTCTL_TXFFLSH);

```
also in the registerdescription is is pointed out that care must be taken when accessing the flush function is the fifo is still in use.
I do not see such test.

4)  silicon defect 
the problem arises when flushing the RXFIFO.
The function times-out and return error.
`
USBx->GRSTCTL = USB_OTG_GRSTCTL_RXFFLSH; 
`
after setting the bit, the hardware does not return the register bit.

According to datasheet after setting the RXFIFO flush bit.
_"""
The application must wait until the bit is cleared before performing any other operations. This
bit requires 8 clocks (slowest of PHY or AHB clock) to clear.
"""_
The bit should be safely cleared within 20000 queries that is implemented.


Hope this helps to improve the driver, regards Adib.



3. The use case that generates the problem.

4. How we can reproduce the problem.


**Additional context**
If you have a first analysis or patch correction, thank you to share your proposal.

comments.body:
Hi @theadib,

Back to you with some updates. Our development teams confirmed almost all the points you reported:
* In the function `USB_HostInit()` and `USB_StopHost()`, the values returned by the FIFO flush functions are not checked.
* In the @brief section of the `USB_FlushTxFifo()`, the function name is incorrect.
* According to REFMAN RM0390, bits `TXFFLSH` and `RXFFLSH`, respectively, must not be set while the core is writing to or reading from the Tx and Rx FIFOs, respectively. Such check is not done.

All these points have been dealt with and fixes will be made available in a future release.

Only one point will be kept unchanged.
* In the function `USB_StopDevice()`, the max number of endpoints is hard-coded (`15U`) while, according to the REFMAN, it depends on the device's part-number.

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/4aba24d78fef03d797a82b258f37dbc84728bbb5/Drivers/STM32F4xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f4xx_ll_usb.c#L1116-L1121

This last point has been confirmed **not** to be an issue and we prefer to keep that approach to ensure all IN and OUT EPs' registers are cleared.

Thank you again for this detailed report.

title: RTOS + USB MSC. Message Queue overflow
body:
**Describe the set-up**
 * STM32F411 Discovery kit
 * FreeRTOS + USB Host + MSC Class + FatFs

**Describe the bug**
The USB driver is putting a way to much in the message queue of the OS. The OS is returning an error code that the memory can't be reserved anymore. All error codes are been ignored from the OS, that's why it is still "working". 

**How To Reproduce**
1. Activate USBH_USE_OS 
2. Set in usbh_def.h MSGQUEUE_OBJECTS to an high value. 250 for example. 
3. You should see that after a while all 250 entries are been used, when an USB is connected. 
3. Another way is to add in cmsis_os.c in the function of osMessagePut(...) an error reaction if xQueueSend wasn't successful. 

**Additional context**

title: template file system_stm32f4xx.c should support userdefined location of vectortable
body:
**Caution**
The Issues are strictly limited for the reporting of problem encountered with the software provided in this project.
For any other problem related to the STM32 product, the performance, the hardware characteristics and boards, the tools the environment in general, please post a topic in the [ST Community/STM32 MCUs forum](https://community.st.com/s/group/0F90X000000AXsASAW/stm32-mcus).

**Describe the set-up**
 * The board (either ST RPN reference or your custom board).
 * IDE or at least the compiler and its version.
Project generated by CubeMX

**Describe the bug**
A clear and concise description of what the bug is.
template file system_stm32f4xx.c should support userdefined location of vectortable
using a custom bootloader requires to move the default location of the vector table.
in the file system_stm32f4xx.c that is copied by the program generator is the needed settings for the move of the vector table.
But the user can not control this behaviour by compiler command arguments
in the defines section at the beginning of the file line 92ff
the lines:
/* #define VECT_TAB_SRAM */
#define VECT_TAB_OFFSET  0x00 /*!< Vector Table base offset field. 
                                   This value must be a multiple of 0x200. */
/******************************************************************************/

have to be changed to
/* #define VECT_TAB_SRAM */
#if !defined(VECT_TAB_OFFSET)
#define VECT_TAB_OFFSET  0x00 /*!< Vector Table base offset field. 
                                   This value must be a multiple of 0x200. */
#endif
/******************************************************************************/

So the user can control the define from compiler command arguments.
This allows targets for bootloader or plain memory layout.

All the existing code will not break.

**How To Reproduce**
1. Indicate the global behavior of your application project.

2. The modules that you suspect to be the cause of the problem (Driver, BSP, MW ...).

3. The use case that generates the problem.

4. How we can reproduce the problem.


**Additional context**
If you have a first analysis or patch correction, thank you to share your proposal.

**Screenshots**
If applicable, add screenshots to help explain your problem.

comments.author: RKOUSTM
comments.body:
Hi @theadib,

Thank you for your contribution. Our development teams confirmed the issue you pointed out. The fix below will be available in the next release. 
```diff
+ #if defined(USER_VECT_TAB_ADDRESS)
/* #define VECT_TAB_SRAM */
+ #if defined(VECT_TAB_SRAM)
+ #define VECT_TAB_BASE_ADDRESS   SRAM_BASE       /*!< Vector Table base address field.
+                                                    This value must be a multiple of 0x200. */
+ #define VECT_TAB_OFFSET         0x00000000U     /*!< Vector Table base offset field.
+                                                    This value must be a multiple of 0x200. */
+ #else
+ #define VECT_TAB_BASE_ADDRESS   FLASH_BASE      /*!< Vector Table base address field.
+                                                     This value must be a multiple of 0x200. */
+ #define VECT_TAB_OFFSET         0x00000000U     /*!< Vector Table base offset field.
+                                                    This value must be a multiple of 0x200. */
+ #endif /* VECT_TAB_SRAM */
+ #endif /* USER_VECT_TAB_ADDRESS */
```

 I hope this answer helps. If you have no other question about this subject, I think this issue can be closed.

With regards,

Hi @RKOUSTM 

In STM32duino, it is possible to redefine `VECT_TAB_OFFSET` to use a bootloader.
In a general way Bootloader is stored at the beginning of the FLASH, in that case the `VECT_TAB_OFFSET` is set to the `SCB->VTOR = FLASH_BASE | VECT_TAB_OFFSET;` where offset is set after the BL.

With the `USER_VECT_TAB_ADDRESS`  I don't understand how we can properly set it as the `VECT_TAB_OFFSET` is always 0.
This only allow to set it to SRAM or FLASH.

title: Ship examples and documentation in separate repositories to reduce checkout size
body:
A checkout of this git repository takes up about 1.4 GB on disk, and cloning it pulls about 150 MB across the net.  Most of this disk and bandwidth is comprised of the example projects, as well as some particularly large documentation files.  There are also some files that seem somewhat unecessary like [this 2 MB bitmap image](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/master/_htmresc/STM32Cube.bmp), and [this 26 MB of audio files](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/tree/master/Utilities/Media/Audio) that will be very infrequently used.

We would like to use this repository as a git submodule within our firmware projects, but this causes problems:
 * Every firmware project we have would take up 1.4 GB on disk, so we'd waste quite a lot of disk space.
 * Our CI pipeline builds will be slowed down by using it.  On a fast connection (Linode box) it currently takes about 12 seconds to pull this repository across the net, and then another 10 seconds to actually unpack it onto disk.  Adding 22s to every CI build slows us down.

Our workaround at the moment is to make a repository of our own with the same structure as this one, with all the extra stuff removed.  This brings the repository size down significantly (to about 11 MB, which takes less than a second to pull across the network), but comes at the expense of making it harder to upgrade to a later version of STM32CubeF4, as we have to go through that process every time.

Please will you consider splitting this repository up into several repositories -- I imagine at least this set:
 * The minimal source for building against (presumably most things in `Drivers` -- the things in `Middlewares` would presumably be better suited in a separate repository anyway, as they are presumably replicated in other STM32CubeF* instances too...)
 * An examples repository
 * Potentially a documentation repository

I use this function (`HAL_I2C_Slave_Receive_IT`) to let the I2C turn to receive IT mode.
That function set the state to HAL_I2C_STATE_BUSY_RX, not HAL_I2C_STATE_BUSY_TX_**LISTEN**
`hi2c->State     = HAL_I2C_STATE_BUSY_RX;`

2. After the Slave transmited all the data, the state must be HAL_I2C_STATE_READY, not HAL_I2C_STATE_LISTEN.
Because the Slave can not transmit data anymore if the hi2c->State is HAL_I2C_STATE_LISTEN.

title: Parenthesis around if body
body:
When macro is used within an if-else statement, it can lead to ambiguities, when not sourrounded by curly braces.

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/5d01400afd60410f6e049cbd19179a67d44d53fd/Middlewares/Third_Party/FreeRTOS/Source/portable/GCC/ARM_CM4F/portmacro.h#L92

A better style would be to write:
```
#define portEND_SWITCHING_ISR( xSwitchRequired ) \
    do \
        { if( xSwitchRequired != pdFALSE ) portYIELD(); \
    } while(0)
```

title: ASSERTION FAILED during RCC initialization with STM32CubeMX + FreeRTOS generated code
body:
In function HAL_RCC_ClockConfig, which in turn is called by SystemClockConfig and main.c from CubeMX generated code (at least when FreeRTOS is using a timer for systick) 

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/5d01400afd60410f6e049cbd19179a67d44d53fd/Drivers/STM32F4xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f4xx_hal_rcc.c#L713

here the default value of uwTickPrio is used, which is set (possibly by intention) to an invalid value:

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/a86ecaa2fb63029596ba7dabadab2d9c2c139560/Drivers/STM32F4xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f4xx_hal.c#L95

This results in some unintended assertion.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7723396/82347746-4eba6900-99f8-11ea-8a8e-e08a29d5074d.png)

In my config, TIM14 is used as the SysTick source.

My hotfix to this issue is, to set uwTickPrio to a valid value in user code section between HAL_Init and SystemClockConfig.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7723396/82348194-d0aa9200-99f8-11ea-98c5-5bd989f9feb5.png)

title: stm32f4xx_hal_rcc.c  line:545  check RCC_PLLCFGR_PLLP  registers error
body:
Hi Community,

I find a bug in STM32CubeF4 Ver 1.25.0  stm32f4xx_hal_rcc.c  line 546.

This wil return HAL_ERROR when the register is correct.

>​        /* Do not return HAL_ERROR if request repeats the current configuration */
>        pll_config = RCC->PLLCFGR;
>        if((READ_BIT(pll_config, RCC_PLLCFGR_PLLSRC) != RCC_OscInitStruct->PLL.PLLSource) ||
>           (READ_BIT(pll_config, RCC_PLLCFGR_PLLM) != RCC_OscInitStruct->PLL.PLLM) ||
>           (READ_BIT(pll_config, RCC_PLLCFGR_PLLN) != RCC_OscInitStruct->PLL.PLLN) ||
>           (READ_BIT(pll_config, RCC_PLLCFGR_PLLP) != RCC_OscInitStruct->PLL.PLLP) ||
>           (READ_BIT(pll_config, RCC_PLLCFGR_PLLQ) != RCC_OscInitStruct->PLL.PLLQ))
>        {
>          return HAL_ERROR;
>        }  

​base on stm32f4xx_hal_rcc.c  line 497:

>​        /* Configure the main PLL clock source, multiplication and division factors. */
>        WRITE_REG(RCC->PLLCFGR, (RCC_OscInitStruct->PLL.PLLSource                                            | \
>                                 RCC_OscInitStruct->PLL.PLLM                                                 | \
>                                 (RCC_OscInitStruct->PLL.PLLN << RCC_PLLCFGR_PLLN_Pos)             | \
>                                 (((RCC_OscInitStruct->PLL.PLLP >> 1U) - 1U) << RCC_PLLCFGR_PLLP_Pos) | \
>                                 (RCC_OscInitStruct->PLL.PLLQ << RCC_PLLCFGR_PLLQ_Pos)));


and stm32f4xx_hal_rcc.h  line 497:

>/** @defgroup RCC_PLLP_Clock_Divider PLLP Clock Divider
>  * @{
>  */
>#define RCC_PLLP_DIV2                  0x00000002U
>#define RCC_PLLP_DIV4                  0x00000004U
>#define RCC_PLLP_DIV6                  0x00000006U
>#define RCC_PLLP_DIV8                  0x00000008U

and RM009 page 164:
​
>Bits 17:16 PLLP: Main PLL (PLL) division factor for main system clock
>Set and cleared by software to control the frequency of the general PLL output clock. These
>bits can be written only if PLL is disabled.
>Caution: The software has to set these bits correctly not to exceed 180 MHz on this domain.
>PLL output clock frequency = VCO frequency / PLLP with PLLP = 2, 4, 6, or 8
>>00: PLLP = 2
>>01: PLLP = 4
>>10: PLLP = 6
>>11: PLLP = 8

stm32f4xx_hal_rcc.c line 546: 
>(READ_BIT(pll_config, RCC_PLLCFGR_PLLP) != RCC_OscInitStruct->PLL.PLLP) ||  

should be replace by :  
>(READ_BIT(pll_config, RCC_PLLCFGR_PLLP) != ((RCC_OscInitStruct->PLL.PLLP >> 1U) - 1U)) ||

comments.author: InconsolableCellist
comments.body:
I believe this is still broken. In `stm32f4xx_hal_rcc.c` on line 553 the `HEAD` in `master` from git shows:

  `          (READ_BIT(pll_config, RCC_PLLCFGR_PLLSRC) != RCC_OscInitStruct->PLL.PLLSource) `

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/2f3b26f16559f7af495727a98253067a31182cfc/Drivers/STM32F4xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f4xx_hal_rcc.c#L553

There was a partial fix in `d599a824d`, but you need to also shift the PLL.PLLSource over by `RCC_PLLCFGR_PLLSRC_Pos` like the other ones, or perhaps better, use `READ_BIT`.

I believe this error may be repeated on lines 545 and 1043, but I didn't check those codepaths.

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/2f3b26f16559f7af495727a98253067a31182cfc/Drivers/STM32F4xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f4xx_hal_rcc.c#L545

https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/2f3b26f16559f7af495727a98253067a31182cfc/Drivers/STM32F4xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f4xx_hal_rcc.c#L1043

----

Additionally, there seems to be a regression introduced by 55c4943bb8 where it returns HAL_ERROR despite a valid PLL config, generated by STM32CubeMX 6.3.0 on the STM32F407 DISC-1 board using the following (and apparently valid) clock configuration: https://i.imgur.com/Bz2ifz1.png

In the latest git version of the code (2f3b26f1, `master` branch) there's a discrepancy between `RCC->PLLCFGR_PLLN` and the requested `RCC_OscInitStruct->PLL.PLLN`. In this case, I'm requesting the valid PLLN of 336 (RM0090 Rev. 19, p. 227), but the old PLLN is something different. The `RCC->PLLCFGR` is never updated by anything (like it is on line 78, but only in the case of it not being a system clock already).

I think the fundamental issue may be that STM32CubeMX is generating init code for using a PLL as a system clock, while the safety checks in that HAL file assume you're on a non-PLL and trying to switch to it--and it only lets you if your configuration is identical to what it was before.

comments.body:
I've found a work around. If I select HSI instead of HSE as a clock source it works. The only problem is that STM32CubeMX says it cannot resolve the clock issues in that case, but it still works if I ignore the error message and proceed to generate code.
HSE is not connected to a crystal, but to an ST-link output. Maybe there is a correlation.

This doesn't resolve the issue in my opinion. Default options should result in a working program. And when the generated code works there shouldn't be an error message complaining it shouldn't work.

comments.author: atsju
comments.body:
Hi @RKOUSTM ,
I agree this is a big workload to make all changes. And yes the API of the HAL will change in that way that the function prototype is slightly different. 
**BUT there is no need to change the examples neither the user code**. Indeed adding this const only says that the function itself will no modify the data but the user buffer could be non const without any compilation warning or issue. The proposed changes  would only make your code cleaner and has absolutely no impact for your customer (I am part of those customers who do not want the API to change). 
Best regards,

comments.author: ghost
comments.body:
I totally agree with @atsju . API-breaking changes must not be avoided, but instead must be introduced in a new major version. You can still maintain your current API with minor revisions and bugfixes for some time e.g.: 18 months by releasing minor versions, while encouraging everyone to move eventually into the safer, const-correct API.
This is mostly what most FOSS libraries out there do (see `mbedtls` or `esp-idf` as examples) in order to keep a good balance between new features, safety and backwards compatibility.

comments.author: jrahlf
comments.body:
Hi @RKOUSTM, 

As said by @atsju, adding const to function parameters does not break any API. It merely informs the caller that the function will not / cannot modify the callers' parameters.

Hence I find this decision **outrageous**, especially since it is very easy to implement from a technical point of view. Give any intern a few weeks and he will do it for you. It is almost impossible to screw it up because the compiler will tell you if do something wrong (unless you start using const casts).

I was really cheering for ST since they opened this public bug tracker and published the STM32Cube pack creator tool, which should boost the STM32 software ecosystem through continuous and transparent improvements.
_But this seems like a big step backwards.._

Also, this has been in your pipeline for several years by now (as mentioned by @ALABSTM). This must be a joke.
This issue should not be closed yet (but all the duplicates should be).

comments.body:
I'm not able to share a schematic, but we have an STM32F412RGT acting as an I2C master using I2C1 on PB8 (SCL) and PB9(SDA).  The clock speed is 400 kHz.  There are three slaves on the bus, and the one we are talking to when the problem occurs is an LIS2HH12TR accelerometer.

As described in the post, I think the problem is that `HAL_I2C_EV_IRQHandler()` can't manage the case where both TXE and BTF are set.  If you can get TXE and BTF set at the same time, you should see the same lockup we're observing.  

Probably you could use some higher priority ISR to inhibit handling the TXE interrupt long enough that BTF is set, too, and then see what happens when `HAL_I2C_EV_IRQHandler()` finally executes.

comments.author: JRASTM
comments.body:
Hi,

Understood the hypothesis, but by double check the handler, in both case RXNE or TXE with a BTF, the most important flag checked is BTF thanks to the last part of if condition of RXNE or TXE.

Here is an extract, you can find that TXE is checked only if BTF is reset, if BTF set it is BTF flag condition that is execute :
if ((I2C_CHECK_FLAG(sr1itflags, I2C_FLAG_TXE) != RESET) && (I2C_CHECK_IT_SOURCE(itsources, I2C_IT_BUF) != RESET) && **(I2C_CHECK_FLAG(sr1itflags, I2C_FLAG_BTF) == RESET)**)

Now by checking the code of hal i2c versus current hal i2c in our development branch, there are some issues corrected around Mem HAL I2C interface.

Like this one in particularity : ST Internal Reference 50144 integrated in version FW package F4 V1.24.2
This bug have been found using hal mem interface in case an error occurs during exchange between slave.

May be an alignement with HAL I2C will solved the issue.

Regards,
Jerome.

comments.author: zacwbond
comments.body:
Hi Jerome,

I agree with what you're saying: if TXE and BTF are both set, then the BTF is what is handled by calling `I2C_MasterTransmit_BTF()`.  My point is that I don't think that's what should happen in the memory read case.

Suppose you do a memory read by calling  `HAL_I2C_Mem_Read_IT()`.  That sets the state to `HAL_I2C_STATE_BUSY_RX`.  The SB and ADDR interrupts get handled properly, so that the next expected interrupt is TXE after the read address is sent.  But if handling of that TXE gets held off, then both BTF and TXE will be set.

When `HAL_I2C_EV_IRQHandler()` is finally called, the conditional that you describe results in the execution of `I2C_MasterTransmit_BTF().`  But because the state is `HAL_I2C_STATE_BUSY_RX`, that function becomes a no-op, the interrupts are not cleared, and they continue recurring forever.

Please explain if I am missing something in this execution sequence.

Thanks,
-Zac

title: UART Baudrate Calculation Error At Clock Higher Than 172MHz
body:
Problem: STM32F407 can not calculate correct baud rate if MCU is overclocked over 171MHz.

UART Baudrate calculation happens in (i.e.) `stm32f4xx_hal_uart.c` in function `UART_SetConfig(UART_HandleTypeDef *huart)`.

Inside this function the following line calculates the `DIV_Mantissa` and `DIV_Fraction` values for the UART `BRR` register, which sets up a clock divider for the serial port to be as close as possible to the desired baud rate clock:

`huart->Instance->BRR = UART_BRR_SAMPLING8(HAL_RCC_GetPCLK2Freq(), huart->Init.BaudRate);`

(There is 16 bit caltulation also, but it is irrelevant for now.)

The function that returns the register value as result is a macro (in `stm32f4xx_hal_uart.h`).
Inside this macro the return value of `HAL_RCC_GetPCLK2Freq()` is multiplied by (uint)25, (uint)100, divided by (uint)100, etc.

The return value of `HAL_RCC_GetPCLK2Freq()` is the system clock frequency in Hz. In a 168MHz environment this is a relatively huge number for the (uint32_t) return type, because this number is later multiplied, divided by the (uint) numbers inside the macro.

My observation is if the system clock frequency is the following:

`UART_BRR_SAMPLING8((uint32_t)171798691, (uint32_t)115200)` returns `2979`,
`UART_BRR_SAMPLING8((uint32_t)171798692, (uint32_t)115200)` returns `0`

This is clearly an overflow, and system clock above 171.8MHz can not calculate the uart baudrate divider.

`UART_BRR_SAMPLING8((uint64_t)171798692, (uint32_t)115200)` returns `2979` again.

Changing the type from 32 bit uint to 64 bit uint of the first parameter fixes this issue, but getting the clock is coded inside the library and `HAL_RCC_GetPCLK2Freq()` return uint32_t.

This might be fixed systemwide by changing the return type of `HAL_RCC_GetPCLK2Freq()` to `uint64_t` or by changing the macro to force type casting for the first input parameter to 64 bit uint (but then this will fix only the uart related problems).

For now I fix this issue by changing the return type of `HAL_RCC_GetPCLK2Freq()` to 64 bit, but later I'd like to use the library updates, so please fix this issue if possible or tell me the reason why this function returns such type that may overflow, and what other method should I use then.

Thank You!

comments.author: GCASTM
comments.body:
Hi @resetcoder 
On STM32F4xx serie, BRR baud rate calculation is specific to U(S)ART IP. Then, problem you raised, will be corrected in all HAL and LL drivers, that are using this peripheral (HAL_UART, HAL_USART, HAL_IRDA and HAL_SMARTCARD + LL_USART).

For HAL UART BRR case, here is the correction i would propose (in stm32f4xx_hal_uart.h) : 
`
#define UART_DIV_SAMPLING16(_PCLK_, _BAUD_)            ((uint32_t)((((uint64_t)(_PCLK_))*25U)/(4U*((uint64_t)(_BAUD_)))))
#define UART_DIVMANT_SAMPLING16(_PCLK_, _BAUD_)        (UART_DIV_SAMPLING16((_PCLK_), (_BAUD_))/100U)
#define UART_DIVFRAQ_SAMPLING16(_PCLK_, _BAUD_)        ((((UART_DIV_SAMPLING16((_PCLK_), (_BAUD_)) - (UART_DIVMANT_SAMPLING16((_PCLK_), (_BAUD_)) * 100U)) * 16U) + 50U) / 100U)
/* UART BRR = mantissa + overflow + fraction
            = (UART DIVMANT << 4) + (UART DIVFRAQ & 0xF0) + (UART DIVFRAQ & 0x0FU) */
#define UART_BRR_SAMPLING16(_PCLK_, _BAUD_)            ((UART_DIVMANT_SAMPLING16((_PCLK_), (_BAUD_)) << 4U) + \
                                                        (UART_DIVFRAQ_SAMPLING16((_PCLK_), (_BAUD_)) & 0xF0U) + \
                                                        (UART_DIVFRAQ_SAMPLING16((_PCLK_), (_BAUD_)) & 0x0FU))

#define UART_DIV_SAMPLING8(_PCLK_, _BAUD_)             ((uint32_t)((((uint64_t)(_PCLK_))*25U)/(2U*((uint64_t)(_BAUD_)))))
#define UART_DIVMANT_SAMPLING8(_PCLK_, _BAUD_)         (UART_DIV_SAMPLING8((_PCLK_), (_BAUD_))/100U)
#define UART_DIVFRAQ_SAMPLING8(_PCLK_, _BAUD_)         ((((UART_DIV_SAMPLING8((_PCLK_), (_BAUD_)) - (UART_DIVMANT_SAMPLING8((_PCLK_), (_BAUD_)) * 100U)) * 8U) + 50U) / 100U)
/* UART BRR = mantissa + overflow + fraction
            = (UART DIVMANT << 4) + ((UART DIVFRAQ & 0xF8) << 1) + (UART DIVFRAQ & 0x07U) */
#define UART_BRR_SAMPLING8(_PCLK_, _BAUD_)             ((UART_DIVMANT_SAMPLING8((_PCLK_), (_BAUD_)) << 4U) + \
                                                        ((UART_DIVFRAQ_SAMPLING8((_PCLK_), (_BAUD_)) & 0xF8U) << 1U) + \
                                                        (UART_DIVFRAQ_SAMPLING8((_PCLK_), (_BAUD_)) & 0x07U))
`

UART_DIV_SAMPLING16 and UART_DIV_SAMPLING8 contains the modification which address the problem. Added parenthesis in UART_BRR_SAMPLING16 and UART_BRR_SAMPLING8 aim to solve MISRA warnings.

To answer your last question on F7, BRR computation in more recent version of USART IP is slightly different, and macros are already able to handle higher frequencies. So no issue on F7/H7 in my opinion.

Any feedback welcome.
Regards
GCA

title: Bit position of TimeFormat in HAL_RTC
body:
I am developing the RTC function with HAL library on STM32F4. There is a confuss on the bit position of timeformat for RTC register operation.

In the source code, the TimeFormat position of HAL_RTC_SetTime is **16**:

![1](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/24732951/64396450-085aef00-d0a1-11e9-8fc6-fddee6e314db.PNG)

Yet in the Reference manual (RM0430, page 760), it says:
![2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/24732951/64396464-114bc080-d0a1-11e9-8c24-122f9d82d9c6.png)

It happens on other functions, such as HAL_RTC_GetTime, HAL_RTC_GetAlarm, HAL_RTC_SetAlarm.
Could you share why the bit position of TimeFormat is 16?

comments.author: ALABSTM
comments.body:
Hi windingcat,

First, let me thank you for your contribution. Actually, both reference manual and RTC HAL driver remain coherent although it may not seem the case at first glance.

Indeed, parameter "TimeFormat" should be assigned one out of the two predefined values listed below:
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/b5abca20c9676b04f8d2885a668a9b653ee65705/Drivers/STM32F4xx_HAL_Driver/Inc/stm32f4xx_hal_rtc.h#L269-L270
As you may notice, constant "RTC_HOURFORMAT12_PM" is defined to be 0x40 which corresponds to a 6-time shift (0x01 << 6).

Added to this the 16-time shift you highlighted, the total yields a 22-time shift, exactly as indicated in the reference manual.
https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeF4/blob/b5abca20c9676b04f8d2885a668a9b653ee65705/Drivers/STM32F4xx_HAL_Driver/Src/stm32f4xx_hal_rtc.c#L750
I agree this might be confusing a little bit but the driver handles this parameter correctly.

I hope this answers your question and thank you once more for pointing out this detail.

With regards,

comments.author: windingcat
comments.body:
hi, ALABSTM, Thanks for your kind response. 
It is good news that it is working well. Although from my side, I prefer to match the hardware manual instead of this trick since there may be extra on maintaining codes.
